facts.fact: Probabilistic models have been previously shown to be efficient and effective for modeling and recognition of human motion.
facts.supporting_span: Probabilistic models have been previously shown to be efficient and effective for modeling and recognition of human motion .

facts.fact: Methods represent the human motion model as a triangulated graph.
facts.supporting_span: In particular we focus on methods which represent the human motion model as a triangulated graph .

facts.fact: Previous approaches learned models based just on positions and velocities of the body parts while ignoring their appearance.

facts.fact: The paper suggests an improved approach for learning such models and using them for human motion recognition.

facts.fact: The suggested approach combines positions, velocities and appearance into both the learning and detection phases.

facts.fact: The suggested hybrid probabilistic model leads to faster convergence of the learning phase.
facts.supporting_span: We show that the suggested hybrid proba-bilistic model (which combines global variables , like translation , with local variables , like relative positions and appearances of body parts) , leads to : (i) faster convergence of learning phase , (ii) robustness to occlusions , and , (iii) higher recognition rate .
